title: Drywall
subtitle: The consequence stays; the confession changes the relationship
sourceCredit: Hope Iyiewuare · The Moth, “Cleanliness Is Next to Mom-liness”

illustration.direction: A narrow modest bedroom in late afternoon. The teen stands in three-quarter profile left of an intact plaster wall, one fist held tensely near his chest and the other hand down, shoulders raised, jaw tight. Both feet visibly bear weight on floorboards; a bed edge, closed door and small cleaning bucket establish the room without crowding the wall. Leave clear negative space between fist and plaster. His anger is private, not heroic violence.

illustration.direction: The teen kneels on the bedroom floor and gathers plaster crumbs with a small brush into a dustpan. His fingers wrap the brush handle, the bristles meet the floor, and his forward knee supports the reach. The parent stays beside him at a modest distance, watching rather than taking over. The damaged wall is still conspicuous and unpatched. The teen's face is sober and determined; ordinary cleanup is the meaningful action.

The same narrow room now feels breathable, with responsibility and connection present together.
